answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond in a scarce resource before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation. The ledger links each bond to one active identity, and proven fraud burns it while honest agents can reclaim theirs on exit. This makes a sybil swarm costly: an attacker must lock up capital for every fake account and risks losing it, rather than creating identities for free. Even a crystal-clear plan to wander through the network under a zephyr of aliases cannot evade that per-identity cost.
